1.why: verify-token requires the reset token’s sessionId to match the caller’s session and rejects mismatched tokens.

2.why: A token is bound to sessionId, so another session/user cannot successfully reuse the same reset code.

3.why: Password reset marks the token used and updates the current session flags but never invalidates other existing sessions in the map.

4.why: Bun serves the app over TLS with certificates, HSTS is set, and a separate HTTP listener issues a 308 redirect to HTTPS.

5.why: Reset codes are stored as SHA-256 hashes and passwords are bcrypt-hashed; protection is hashing/TLS rather than encrypting all user data at rest.

6.why: There is no real email body with account PII; responses stay generic, though the demo returns the raw mock token to the client.

7.why: Inputs are validated with strict helpers (validIdentifier, validToken, validMfa, passwordPolicy) and UI messages use textContent only.

8.why: Redirects are fixed to the local HTTPS origin or same-site paths like /verify; no user-controlled open redirect exists.

9.why: No email HTML template incorporates user input; delivery is a client-side mock log without script injection.

10.why: mockToken/mockMfaCode are returned by the API and written into the on-page Logs panel, so tokens do appear in logs.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed in memory, but MOCK_MFA_CODE is hardcoded in source and session MFA uses that fixed secret.

12.why: No classic default username/password login exists, yet the fixed mock MFA code 482916 acts as a standing default secret.

13.why: Server-side rate limits cap recovery requests and failed token/MFA verifications (e.g., 3 and 5 attempts per window).

14.why: recovery-request always returns the same non-enumerating message regardless of whether the identifier would match an account.

15.why: Reset codes come from randomBytes(32) base64url values, are stored hashed, expire, and are bound to the requesting session.
